layer_map.what: BodyEditor owns the `editing` boolean (local `useState`, default preview; **reset→preview on `activeTabId` change via a render-phase `useState`-prev compare — hold `prevTab` in `useState(activeTabId)` and, when `activeTabId !== prevTab`, call `setPrevTab(activeTabId)` + `setEditing(false)` during render (same commit as the tab switch, render stays pure); NOT a ref written during render (not rolled back on a discarded StrictMode/concurrent retry) and NOT a passive `useEffect` (paints a one-frame edit-mode flash) — AC-6**); renders the edit/preview toggle button in the toolbar right slot beside the lang-pill; the toggle's `onMouseDown` calls `preventDefault()` (F-002) so clicking it while editing does not blur the textarea; wires the toggle + passes `editing`/`onEditingChange` to CodeEditor. `handleLangCycle` continues to change `lang` in preview with no editing transition (F-001 must cover this)

CodeEditor gains `editing`/`onEditingChange` props; mounts textarea XOR pre; **tokenizes via a `{value,lang}` snapshot-cache gate evaluated only while the pre is the mounted layer** (F-001) — reuses 018's `colored.snapshot===value` gate extended with `lang`, removes the 100ms debounce effect and the `showColored` null-snapshot degrade-flash; caret-at-click (coordinate→offset, post-mount `setSelectionRange`) + preview focus/Enter-Space entry; **a shared focus-on-mount `useEffect` keyed on `editing` moves focus to the freshly-mounted textarea on EVERY `editing` false→true transition (click, keyboard Enter/Space, toggle button) — `textareaRef.current?.focus()`; the click path additionally applies the stashed caret offset via `setSelectionRange`, keyboard/toggle take focus only (AC-18 keyboard operability)**; blur exit AND toggle exit both drive `onEditingChange(false)` idempotently (F-002); **a toggle switches the mounted layer, and a freshly-mounted textarea/pre begins at `scrollTop=0` — so scroll resets to 0 on every edit↔preview toggle with no capture ref, no restore effect, no ordering machinery**; the `resetKey` reset (zero scroll on tab-switch, AC-6) stays a plain passive `useEffect`; removes `handleTextareaScroll`; classes via `cx()` (no inline styles); keeps 20.625px `--code-line-h` on the single visible layer
jsonTokens.compose() reused byte-unchanged (consumed, NOT modified — incl. its JSON.parse malformed-degrade detector at :363-366); cx() composes toggle-state class tokens

Split AC-9/12/13 line-box co-read into edit-state (textarea) + preview-state (pre) reads; add toggle/click-to-edit/caret/entry coverage; **add F-002 CT (click toggle while editing → lands in preview)**; add a toggle CT asserting the freshly-mounted layer reads `scrollTop===0` (scroll resets on toggle, as designed); add the AC-6 switch-tab-while-editing CT (immediate post-switch read is preview/`body-pre`, not textarea — no intermediate edit-mode frame); add F-001 first-mount/tab-switch/lang-cycle preview-recolor assertions; drop 018 colored-during-edit assertions; testids → only-visible-layer
CodeEditor description: three-layer overlay → edit/preview toggle (editing prop, tokenize-on-preview via snapshot-cache gate)

key_design_decisions.chosen_approach: Compose runs when the pre is the mounted layer AND the `{value,lang}` snapshot-cache is stale — reuses 018's `colored.snapshot===value` gate (CodeEditor.tsx:124) extended to also key on `lang`; derive synchronously in a `useMemo` gated so `compose()` is invoked only when `!editing`. Remove the 100ms debounce effect and the `showColored` null-degrade flash
key_design_decisions.why: One rule covers AC-14 (compose unreachable while editing — the pre is unmounted, so no per-keystroke compose, respecting §6 highlight-while-typing exclusion), AC-17 (first preview mount composes), AC-6 (new `value` on tab-switch composes), and lang-cycle-in-preview (new `lang` composes). Reuses the existing snapshot cache (§6.3 search-before-building; §3.6 DRY) — NOT a new pattern; extending the key with `lang` folds in what the deleted debounce's `[value,lang]` deps used to cover. Collapses 018's `colored===null` degrade-flash branch (no AC exercised it — plain-degrade lives inside compose per AC-4), so no null state remains
key_design_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Fire compose only on the edit→preview transition (prior draft): misses first-mount/tab-switch/lang-cycle (AC-17/AC-6) — the confirmed F-001 defect. Naive `useMemo([value,lang])` ungated: recomputes per keystroke while editing — violates AC-14 and §6

key_design_decisions.chosen_approach: `onMouseDown → e.preventDefault()` on the toolbar toggle button so clicking it while editing does not blur the textarea; the single `onClick` owns the flip (reads current `editing`), while textarea `blur` remains an independent exit that calls `onEditingChange(false)`
key_design_decisions.why: Suppressing the button's focus-steal removes the mousedown-blur-then-click double-fire that left the toggle dead while editing (AC-16). Minimal, standard toolbar-button-over-editor pattern; keeps the toggle a true flip and both exits idempotent-toward-false. Establishes the toggle affordance's event convention (no prior established pattern for this concern — not a flagged departure)
key_design_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Coalesce both signals into idempotent-toward-false + read `editing` at click without preventDefault: more moving parts, still lets the button steal focus mid-edit; harder to reason about ordering. No handling (prior draft): the confirmed F-002 dead-toggle defect

key_design_decisions.chosen_approach: Reset the code-area scroll to (0,0) on every edit↔preview toggle. Mechanism: conditional-mount already swaps the mounted layer on a toggle, and a freshly-mounted textarea/pre begins at `scrollTop=0`/`scrollLeft=0` — so the reset is the natural mount behavior. NO capture ref, NO restore `useLayoutEffect`, NO effect-ordering. Tab-switch scroll reset (AC-6) is split by path. On a **tab-switch-WHILE-EDITING** the pre does NOT persist — BodyEditor's render-phase reset forces `editing→false` atomically (see the "Tab-switch → preview" decision), so the pre **fresh-mounts at `scrollTop=0`** exactly like the toggle case (no effect needed to zero it). On a **preview→preview switch** the pre persists (same node, new content), and there the `resetKey` reset — a plain passive `useEffect` — zeros its scroll (no restore left to race). The earlier "the pre persists across a tab switch" claim was false for the editing path and is corrected here: persistence holds only preview→preview
key_design_decisions.why: Simplest possible correct behavior after descoping scroll-retention: zeroing on toggle is what an unmodified conditional mount already does, so the "decision" is to add nothing. Removes the capture ref (and its null / non-null states), the restore layout-effect, and all F-003 declaration-order machinery — a net deletion (§3.6 KISS, §6.1 Minimal). Scroll-position preservation across a same-tab toggle round-trip is not an AC and is spec Q-2 (OPTIONAL, left open); after three `/grill` cycles in this family the human gate escalated to descope rather than a 4th fix cycle. Reset-to-0-on-toggle introduces NO new feature (§6-respecting): it is the absence of retention, not new behavior
key_design_decisions.alternatives_rejected: **Capture scroll across toggle** (prior draft: stash `{scrollTop,scrollLeft}` in a ref at switch, restore in a layout-effect, `focus({preventScroll:true})`): descoped — retention is an optional Q-2 nicety, not an AC, and it repeatedly bred cross-effect/cross-component ordering defects (three grill cycles). **F-003 scroll-restore ordering** (convert the `resetKey` reset to a `useLayoutEffect` declared before the restore): the entire ordering fix exists only to sequence a restore against the reset — with no restore, it is dead machinery; removed

key_design_decisions.chosen_approach: Conditional-mount: render textarea XOR pre, never both
key_design_decisions.why: AC-10/AC-11 (only visible layer + its testid); sheds overlay stack, debounce, scroll-sync, snapshot (§3.6 KISS). Spec-mandated replacement of the 018 both-mounted overlay (AC-10 is the feature's purpose) — an explicit spec-level replacement, not a discretionary departure
key_design_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Keep both mounted + toggle visibility: retains dead overlay complexity; violates AC-10/AC-11 + KISS

key_design_decisions.chosen_approach: BodyEditor local `useState`; CodeEditor is a controlled molecule (`editing` prop + `onEditingChange`)
key_design_decisions.why: §2.2 organism→molecule one-way + molecules hold NO store awareness; §7 (ephemeral UI state, NOT a tabsStore domain field); matches existing controlled-molecule pattern (Tabs). AC-3/AC-16/AC-17. `editing=true` (edit) exercised by AC-12/AC-15; `editing=false` (preview) by AC-10/AC-14/AC-17 — both mapped
key_design_decisions.alternatives_rejected: `editing` in tabsStore: violates §7 (raw text still round-trips via `updateActiveSpec` unchanged). CodeEditor owning it internally: organism can't keep the toolbar toggle in sync

key_design_decisions.chosen_approach: BodyEditor resets `editing→false` in the SAME commit as the `activeTabId` change using React's documented set-state-in-render idiom — store the previous tab id in **`useState`** (not a ref): `const [prevTab, setPrevTab] = useState(activeTabId); if (activeTabId !== prevTab) { setPrevTab(activeTabId); setEditing(false) }`. React re-renders synchronously before committing/painting, so the swap to preview is atomic with the tab switch — no passive second commit, no intermediate textarea frame. Seeding `useState(activeTabId)` self-initializes `prevTab` on first render, so there is no spurious first-mount reset. Render stays pure — no side effect (no ref write) during render. The FORBIDDEN forms are a `prevActiveTabId` **ref** written during render, and a passive `useEffect(() => setEditing(false), [activeTabId])`
key_design_decisions.why: AC-6 (§5 MANDATORY) has TWO obligations — reset scroll AND return to preview. The return-to-preview obligation is an `editing` mode change (textarea↔pre) owned by BodyEditor, independent of the descoped Q-2 scroll-retention. On the tab-switch-WHILE-EDITING path the pre is unmounted, so return-to-preview requires BodyEditor to flip `editing` in-phase; the `useState`-prev compare is React's documented/ESLint-valid `set-state-in-render` idiom for exactly this, and — unlike a ref — a `useState` update in a render pass React discards and retries IS rolled back, so it reconciles correctly under React 19 StrictMode double-invoke / concurrent throw-away-and-retry. `editing` already lives in BodyEditor, which already subscribes to `activeTabId` (BodyEditor.tsx:63) and passes `resetKey={activeTabId}` (:187) — so the reset is same-component, same-commit with no new wiring. For preview→preview switches `setEditing(false)` bails out (already false), so no extra render there
key_design_decisions.alternatives_rejected: **(a) `prevActiveTabId` ref written during render** (prior cycle-4 form, F-001 CONFIRMED): a ref mutation performed in a render pass React discards/retries is NOT rolled back, so under StrictMode double-invoke / concurrent retry the ref advances to `activeTabId` on a thrown-away pass while the paired `setEditing(false)` is skipped on the retry — silently breaking the AC-6 return-to-preview reset; a bare `useRef` also forces a spurious first-mount reset. **(b) Key/remount CodeEditor by `activeTabId`**: does NOT reset BodyEditor's `editing` (it is BodyEditor-owned per §2.2); making it work forces `editing` into a keyed subtree — pushing ownership into CodeEditor (breaks the controlled-molecule + toolbar-sync) or adding a wrapper solely to host keyed state (§3.6 indirection). **(c) `useLayoutEffect` keyed on `activeTabId`**: fires pre-paint so it also avoids the flash, but it is a second render pass where a render-phase compare needs none — more work for the same result

key_design_decisions.chosen_approach: A single **focus-on-mount `useEffect` keyed on `editing`** that, on the `editing` false→true transition, calls `textareaRef.current?.focus()` — the shared step for ALL three entry paths (caret-at-click, keyboard Enter/Space, toggle button). The click path additionally applies `setSelectionRange` (caret placement) post-mount from a stashed click offset; keyboard/toggle entry take focus only (caret at browser default). Keyed on `editing` alone — NO `editingViaClick` flag
key_design_decisions.why: Conditional-mount UNMOUNTS the focused `pre` and mounts a fresh textarea on entry; nothing else focuses it. On the click path the caret helper focuses it, but keyboard-Enter (the `pre` was the focused element, now unmounted) and toggle-button entry (F-002's `onMouseDown → preventDefault` deliberately suppresses the button's focus-steal, plan §Key Design Decisions "Toggle-exit race") both drop focus to `document.body` — a keyboard user who "entered edit mode" cannot type, defeating AC-18 operability even though `editing===true` passes a naive mount check (confirmed grill finding). Focus is the COMMON obligation across all paths, so it belongs in one effect keyed on the transition, not duplicated per path. `focus()` is idempotent (focusing an already-focused element is a no-op), so no `editingViaClick` gate is needed and no double-focus occurs — the click path no longer calls `focus()` itself, only `setSelectionRange`. Standard React focus-on-mount pattern (§3.6 KISS; no convention departure)
key_design_decisions.alternatives_rejected: **(a) Focus only in the click path** (prior cycle-5 form — CONFIRMED grill finding): leaves keyboard/toggle entry unfocused → AC-18 keyboard-operability gap. **(b) `autoFocus` attribute on the conditionally-mounted textarea**: fires on each fresh mount so it technically focuses all paths, BUT it is mount-time-only, still needs a separate post-mount `setSelectionRange` for the caret (no co-location win), is flagged by `jsx-a11y/no-autofocus`, and is harder to assert in a CT than an explicit `focus()` — rejected for testability + co-location. **(c) `editing && !editingViaClick`-gated effect + click path keeps its own `focus()`**: adds a second state flag with no AC exercising it (§3.6) to avoid a harmless no-op double-focus — rejected

key_design_decisions.chosen_approach: `caretPositionFromPoint` on the pre → Range-from-start length → offset stashed at click, then `setSelectionRange` applied in the post-mount effect flow; **focus is provided by the shared focus-on-entry effect (see "Focus on edit entry") — the click path owns ONLY the caret offset, not the focus call**; clamp offset to `[0, value.length]`, null hit → end-of-text
key_design_decisions.why: AC-12/AC-13; textarea is unmounted at click time so native focus/caret can't be placed synchronously — post-mount mapping is the only option (research Q-1). Focus is the shared step across all entry paths (factored into the focus-on-entry effect); caret placement is the click-path extra. No repo canonical exists → ESTABLISHES the convention (not a departure)
key_design_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Native `textarea.focus()` only: fails AC-12 (textarea not mounted at click). Click path re-calling `focus()` itself: redundant with the shared effect (harmless no-op) — folded into the shared effect for one focus owner

key_design_decisions.chosen_approach: Preview region focusable (tabIndex) + Enter/Space enters edit; **on entry the shared focus-on-entry effect moves focus to the freshly-mounted textarea (keyboard/toggle paths take focus only — no caret offset)**; escaped-children token insertion kept (never innerHTML)
key_design_decisions.why: AC-18 requires keyboard OPERABILITY, not just the mode flip: after Enter/Space unmounts the focused `pre`, focus must land on the textarea or the user is stranded (confirmed grill finding). The focus-on-entry effect satisfies this for keyboard and toggle paths identically to click. AC-8 (no innerHTML). Establishes entry-affordance convention for this surface
key_design_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Click-only entry: fails AC-18 for keyboard users. Focus moved only in the click path (prior form): keyboard/toggle entry leaves focus on `document.body` → AC-18 operability gap

key_design_decisions.chosen_approach: One scroll container; both states bind the same `--code-line-h`=20.625px calc + identical font/padding/box-sizing; drop absolute-overlay CSS
key_design_decisions.why: AC-9/AC-19 (gutter tracks visible layer, one line-box both states); AC-22 (no em row height)
key_design_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Per-state independent metrics: risks row-height drift between edit/preview (§9 Risk)

file_impact.what_changes: Add `editing`/`onEditingChange` props; conditional textarea XOR pre mount; **F-001 `{value,lang}` snapshot-cache `useMemo` gated to `!editing`** (extends the 018 `colored.snapshot===value` gate; deletes the debounce effect + `showColored` null-degrade flash); **a focus-on-mount `useEffect` keyed on `editing` (co-located with the existing `:77`/`:94` effect patterns) that calls `textareaRef.current?.focus()` (`:72`) on every `editing` false→true transition — focuses the freshly-mounted textarea on ALL entry paths (click/keyboard/toggle) so AC-18 keyboard operability holds; keyed on `editing` alone, NO `editingViaClick` flag**; caret-at-click mapping helper (**click path stashes the mapped offset and applies `setSelectionRange` post-mount; focus itself is the shared effect's job, not the caret helper's**); preview focus/Enter-Space entry; **F-002 blur + toggle both drive `onEditingChange(false)` idempotently**; **scroll resets to 0 on toggle via the natural fresh-mount of the swapped layer — NO capture ref, NO restore layout-effect, NO ordering machinery; the `resetKey` reset stays a plain passive `useEffect` (zeros the persistent pre's scroll on tab-switch, AC-6)**; delete `handleTextareaScroll`

Explicitly NOT a `prevActiveTabId` ref written during render and NOT `useEffect(() => setEditing(false), [activeTabId])`**; toolbar toggle button (data-testid `body-edit-toggle`) with **`onMouseDown` preventDefault (F-002)**; pass `editing`/`onEditingChange` to `<CodeEditor>` at :186

Toggle button + editing ownership; **F-002 CT** (click toggle while editing → lands in preview); toggle-resets-scroll CT (toggle, assert the freshly-mounted layer reads scrollTop===0); **toggle-entry focus CT: from preview, click `body-edit-toggle` → assert `document.activeElement` is the mounted textarea (toggle entry focuses the textarea despite F-002 `preventDefault` — AC-18)**; **AC-6 tab-switch-while-editing CT: enter edit (textarea mounted), change `activeTabId`, then in the IMMEDIATE post-switch read assert `body-pre` is mounted and the textarea is NOT — proving the same-commit editing reset (no intermediate edit-mode frame; the forbidden passive-`useEffect` form would commit `editing=true`/textarea for the new tab first)**; only-visible-layer testid assertions

doc_impact.what_changes: Rewrite the CodeEditor molecule description from "three-layer overlay code editor" to an edit/preview toggle: editing prop owned by BodyEditor, single-layer conditional mount, tokenize-on-preview via a `{value,lang}` snapshot-cache gate

risks.risk: `editing` leaks into tabsStore, or CodeEditor imports a store — breaks §2.2 + §7
risks.mitigation: Keep `editing` as BodyEditor `useState`; CodeEditor stays a pure controlled molecule; assert no store import in CodeEditor

risks.risk: F-002 `preventDefault` on toggle mousedown suppresses more than the blur (e.g. blocks button activation needed for AC-18 keyboard path)
risks.mitigation: `preventDefault` on mousedown only cancels focus-shift, not click/keyboard activation; the toggle's keyboard entry stays native; CT pins click-while-editing → preview AND keyboard toggle

risks.risk: AC-6 return-to-preview mis-implemented — reverting to a `prevActiveTabId` **ref** written during render (not rolled back on a discarded StrictMode/concurrent retry → `setEditing(false)` silently skipped) or to a passive `useEffect(() => setEditing(false), [activeTabId])` (editing-flip splits into a second commit → one-frame edit-mode flash of the new tab's raw text)
risks.mitigation: Reset `editing` in the render phase via a `useState`-prev compare (`prevTab` seeded from `useState(activeTabId)`; on `activeTabId !== prevTab` → `setPrevTab` + `setEditing(false)`, same commit as the tab switch, correctly reconciled under StrictMode/concurrent retry); CT switches tabs FROM an editing state and asserts the IMMEDIATE post-switch mounted layer is the pre (preview), catching the transient flash — not only the settled state

risks.risk: F-001 `useMemo` gate recomputes compose while editing if the `!editing` guard is mis-wired
risks.mitigation: Guard invokes `compose()` only when `!editing` AND `{value,lang}` cache stale; pre is unmounted while editing so the path is doubly unreachable; CT asserts no recolor on keystroke-in-edit

risks.risk: compose() "tidied" during the touch, altering the JSON.parse degrade detector
risks.mitigation: §6 OOS + §7 hard constraint — reused byte-unchanged; MEMORY jsonTokens-jsonparse lesson (the pre-validation IS the AC-4 malformed detector)

risks.risk: Line-box row height drifts between edit and preview states
risks.mitigation: Both states bind the same `--code-line-h` + identical font/padding/box-sizing; DOM-verify equal row heights per state (§9 spec risk 1/5)

risks.risk: CodeEditor/BodyEditor Playwright CT cannot mount locally (pre-existing harness break)
risks.mitigation: Verify statically + live-verify per 018; leave test:ct Done-When UNVERIFIED rather than burning repair rounds; reproduce tokens.css import + data-mstyle + production className scope in fixtures (MEMORY)

risks.risk: CT AC-9/12/13 line-box co-read breaks once only one layer mounts at a time
risks.mitigation: Split the assertion into an edit-state (textarea) read and a preview-state (pre) read; both equal the shared line-box height

risks.risk: Focus not moved to the freshly-mounted textarea on a NON-click edit entry (keyboard Enter/Space or toggle button) — conditional-mount unmounts the focused `pre` and F-002's `preventDefault` suppresses the toggle's focus-steal, so focus falls to `document.body` and the keyboard user cannot type (AC-18 operability gap; a naive "textarea mounted" check still passes)
risks.mitigation: A shared focus-on-mount `useEffect` keyed on `editing` calls `textareaRef.current?.focus()` on EVERY false→true transition (owns focus for all three paths; click path adds only `setSelectionRange`); CTs assert `document.activeElement === textareaRef.current` after keyboard-Enter entry AND after toggle-button entry — verifying operability, not just the mode flip

specialist_consultation.input_summary: F-001 reuses 018 snapshot-cache gate extended with lang (verified CodeEditor.tsx:124); F-002 onMouseDown preventDefault; F-003 ref-clear in resetKey effect. No §6 escalation, no departure

specialist_consultation.sub_question: Correct the F-003 scroll-restore ordering defect (passive-useEffect ref-clear ran after the layout-effect restore)
specialist_consultation.input_summary: Convert the resetKey reset to a `useLayoutEffect` declared BEFORE the restore `useLayoutEffect` → deterministic pre-paint precedence (later descoped)

specialist_consultation.sub_question: Author the descope: remove scroll-retention (capture ref + restore useLayoutEffect + F-003 ordering) per the user's bounded-loop escalation decision
specialist_consultation.input_summary: Reset scroll to 0 on every toggle via the natural fresh-mount of the swapped layer (no ref, no restore effect, no ordering); the resetKey reset stays a plain passive useEffect for tab-switch (pre persists, AC-6). F-001/F-002 untouched; strictly simpler (net deletion); §2.2/§3.6/§6.1 compliant; AC-6/AC-19 satisfied; §6-respecting

specialist_consultation.sub_question: Correct the confirmed grill F-001: swap the AC-6 return-to-preview reset from a render-written `prevActiveTabId` ref to the documented `useState`-prev idiom, keeping the same-commit render-phase strategy
specialist_consultation.input_summary: Store prev tab in `useState(activeTabId)`; on `activeTabId !== prevTab` → `setPrevTab(activeTabId)` + `setEditing(false)` during render. Unlike a ref, a `useState` update on a discarded render is rolled back → correct under React 19 StrictMode double-invoke / concurrent retry; render stays pure; `useState`-seeded prev removes the spurious first-mount reset. Strategy (atomic same-commit editing→false) UNCHANGED — only ref→useState mechanism changes. §2.2/§7 compliant (ephemeral BodyEditor state, no store), no §6 over-reach, documented idiom → no convention departure; F-001/F-002/scroll-descope untouched; AC-6/AC-17 satisfied

specialist_consultation.sub_question: Confirm the focus-on-mount-effect fix for the confirmed grill finding (focus not moved to textarea on non-click edit entry); decide whether to key the effect on `editing` alone or `editing && !editingViaClick`
specialist_consultation.input_summary: A shared focus-on-mount `useEffect` keyed on `editing` owns `textareaRef.current?.focus()` for ALL three entry paths (click/keyboard/toggle); the click path owns ONLY the caret offset (`setSelectionRange` post-mount), so focus is the common step and caret is the click-path extra. Keyed on `editing` alone — `focus()` is idempotent, so no `editingViaClick` gate is needed (rejected as an unstated state, Rule 9/§3.6); `autoFocus` rejected (jsx-a11y warning + no caret co-location + weaker testability). Renderer atomic-design + controlled-state scope, AC-18 core (not §6 OOS), standard React pattern → no §2.2/§7 violation, no convention departure. F-001/F-002/scroll-descope/AC-6 useState-prev untouched

dependencies: None — no packages to install, no services to configure, no environment variables. Uses only the native `textarea`, standard DOM caret APIs (`caretPositionFromPoint` / `caretRangeFromPoint`, present in Electron's Chromium renderer), and the already-present `jsonTokens.compose()` + `cx()`.
